decisions.group_label: PMC10127522 (Martinez Steele et al., J Nutr 2022;153(1):225-241) table footnote 5 (row 'Other processed culinary ingredients')
decisions.clause: unsweetened baking chocolate, cocoa powder and gelatin powder
decisions.named: exact term IS named, WITH the condition 'unsweetened' (sweetened cocoa mixes are not covered)
decisions.condition: unsweetened: an item whose own name or bracket adds sugar must not take the Group 2 placement; the item-level mechanism (as for nuts and seeds) is NOT built for this kind yet, so this proposal needs it before it can merge
decisions.reason: OWNER DECISION (2026-11-21): PARK until an item-level 'unsweetened' condition mechanism exists for this kind (like nut_seed). PMC10127522 fn5 places 'unsweetened baking chocolate, cocoa powder and gelatin powder' (exact-named, condition 'unsweetened'). Do not stage the row without the mechanism.

decisions.clause: Processed culinary ingredients are substances extracted from foods of the first group by physical procedures such as pressing, centrifugation, and concentration
decisions.named: exact term not named (class-instance inference: cocoa butter is a fat pressed from cocoa beans); FDC names 'Oil, cocoa butter' (sr_legacy 171421; naming only)

decisions.group_label: PMC10127522 (Martinez Steele et al., J Nutr 2022;153(1):225-241) table footnote 2 (row 'Other unprocessed or minimally processed foods')
decisions.clause: dried fruits (without added sugars) and vegetables
decisions.named: exact term not named (a class phrase covering dried fruit and, in Indian use, nuts); kind nut_seed so the item-level salt/sugar condition applies (the clause is conditioned 'without added sugars'; the nut clause is 'no added salt or sugar')
decisions.reason: OWNER DECISION (2026-11-21): PARK. The clause covers 'dried fruits (without added sugars)', a dried-FRUIT class with a sugar condition; kind nut_seed is a stretch and there is no dried-fruit condition mechanism. Revisit together with the cocoa powder mechanism.

decisions.clause: legumes such as beans, lentils, and chickpeas
decisions.named: exact term not named (class-instance inference: gram is a pulse; FDC names 'bengal gram' as chickpea; roasting is a process named in the Group 1 definition on p.6); every pulse is Group 1, so the ambiguity between bengal, green and black gram does not change the placement

decisions.clause: Vegetable oils crushed from seeds, nuts or fruit (notably olives)
decisions.named: exact term not named (class-instance: an oil; the plant is not stated on the label, which does not change the Group 2 placement of culinary oils)

decisions.clause: butter and lard obtained from milk and pork
decisions.named: exact term not named (class-instance inference: a fat obtained from butter; whether it is anhydrous milk fat or ghee is not stated)

decisions.clause: Fresh, squeezed, chilled, frozen, or dried fruit and leafy and root vegetables
decisions.named: exact term not named (a class phrase: dried vegetables are named; 'dehydrated' read as dried is a definitional step; the contents are unstated, so this is a class-level row)

decisions.clause: sugar and molasses obtained from cane or beet
decisions.named: exact term not named (same ingredient, fine granulation form: an inference; FDC names 'Sugars, granulated' and powdered forms, naming only)

decisions.clause: varieties of sugars (fructose, high-fructose corn syrup
decisions.reason: OWNER AMENDMENT (2026-11-21): HELD (not parked, not staged). Gap: no ingredient-level naming in an admissible source; product-level coding alone insufficient. FAO p.9 names specific sugar varieties (fructose, HFCS, 'fruit juice concentrates', invert sugar, maltodextrin, dextrose, lactose), a named list, not 'all sugars'; Monteiro 2019 (PMC10260459) repeats it; PMC10127522 fn12 'all syrups (excluding 100% maple syrup)' is product-level NHANES coding, corroboration only when a source applies it to ingredients. Bring back only as a fresh proposal if an admissible primary clause names the ingredient form itself.

decisions.clause: varieties of sugars (fructose, high-fructose corn syrup
decisions.reason: OWNER AMENDMENT (2026-11-21): HELD (not parked, not staged). Gap: no ingredient-level naming in an admissible source; product-level coding alone insufficient. FAO p.9 names specific sugar varieties (fructose, HFCS, 'fruit juice concentrates', invert sugar, maltodextrin, dextrose, lactose), a named list, not 'all sugars'; Monteiro 2019 (PMC10260459) repeats it; PMC10127522 fn12 'all syrups (excluding 100% maple syrup)' is product-level NHANES coding, corroboration only when a source applies it to ingredients. Bring back only as a fresh proposal if an admissible primary clause names the ingredient form itself.

OWNER AMENDMENT (2026-11-21): HELD (not parked, not staged). Gap: class membership not established for the texturized form. NUPENS and Lancet 2025 name 'protein isolates or concentrates', but texturizing does not establish an isolate or concentrate (common TVP is texturized soy flour, ~50% protein); no reachable admissible source names texturized/textured protein. Bring back only as a fresh proposal if an admissible primary clause names the ingredient form itself.

PMC10127522 (Martinez Steele et al., J Nutr 2022;153(1):225-241) (footnote 2) places generic 'flours' with the unprocessed or minimally processed foods, while Monteiro et al., Lancet 2025 'Ultra-processed foods and human health: the main thesis and the evidence' (fsp.usp.br PDF) describes ultra-processed foods as made from soy and other crops fractioned into starches, fibre, sugars, oils and fats, and proteins, and NUPENS 'Food classification Nova' page (nupens.fsp.usp.br/en/food-classification-nova/) lists protein isolates or concentrates among group 4 substances: a defatted soy fraction is placed differently depending on which statement applies. FLAGGED, not parked and not staged.
